summary: Lexy, arriving late at the Enderby house, is met by the parlor maid Annie and taken to Mrs. Enderby, who has been writing at her desk. Lexy is torn between a promise not to mention Caroline's absence and her wish to tell the truth to Mrs. Enderby and a young man who trusted her. Mrs. Enderby leads Lexy to Caroline's room, locks the door, and orders Lexy to wear Caroline's hat, coat and veil and leave the house with her, so that Lexy will be taken for Caroline. Lexy refuses in desperation, feeling entangled in promises, obligations and deceptions.
one_line: Lexy, bound by a promise about Caroline's absence, is ordered by Mrs. Enderby to impersonate Caroline and leave the house.
key_facts: Lexy arrives at the Enderbys house more than half an hour late after the time she was asked to return.
Annie, the parlor maid, has been with the Enderby family for nearly ten years and looks disapproving of Lexy's lateness.
Lexy feels she cannot ask anyone anything without breaking a promise to somebody else.
Lexy's one clear resolution is to be freed from her promise not to mention Caroline's absence.
Lexy respects Mrs. Enderby and is a little afraid of her, feeling young, crude and blundering in her presence.
Lexy plans to first get Mrs. Enderby to release her from the promise, then tell the young man, then return and tell Mrs. Enderby.
Mrs. Enderby is writing at her desk when Lexy enters her sitting room and says, "You are late."
Mrs. Enderby leads Lexy to Caroline's room and locks the door on the inside.
Mrs. Enderby says "In fifteen minutes the car is coming."
Mrs. Enderby instructs Lexy to put on Caroline's hat and coat and a veil and leave the house with her.
Mrs. Enderby says she wishes it to be thought that Lexy is Caroline.
Lexy cries "Mrs. Enderby, I—I can't do it!"
Mrs. Enderby replies, "You can, Miss Moran, and I think you will."
Lexy's honest and vigorous spirit is entangled in a network of promises, obligations and deceptions.
